headline: PM orders nationwide flood alert amid worsening waterlogging
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman directs field administration to prioritize lives and property, ensuring swift relief and medical services for affected populations.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has ordered a nationwide alert to protect the lives and property of people affected by severe waterlogging caused by heavy rains. During a virtual meeting with field officials, he emphasized that protecting citizens must be the administration's top priority.

The Prime Minister directed officials to ensure the prompt distribution of dry food, safe drinking water, baby food, essential medicines, and medical care. He specifically instructed that the healthcare and safety of women, children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities be prioritized.

Law enforcement agencies have been placed on maximum alert to maintain law and order. The PM warned that no group should be allowed to exploit the disaster through theft, robbery, hoarding, or the misappropriation of relief materials.

While officials from Chattogram reported that waterlogging is gradually easing, the situation in the Sylhet region is deteriorating due to a damaged embankment along the Manu River. Rangpur Division also faces a high risk of fresh waterlogging.

The Prime Minister stressed the need for transparency and accountability in relief distribution, urging officials to prioritize those genuinely affected. He ordered all authorities to keep personnel and equipment ready for every possible risk.
caption:
Nationwide flood alert! PM Tarique Rahman orders maximum vigilance to protect lives and property amid worsening waterlogging.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has ordered a nationwide alert to protect the lives and property of people affected by severe waterlogging caused by heavy rains. During a virtual meeting with field officials, he emphasized that protecting citizens must be the administration's top priority.

The Prime Minister directed officials to ensure the prompt distribution of dry food, safe drinking water, baby food, essential medicines, and medical care. He specifically instructed that the healthcare and safety of women, children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities be prioritized.

Law enforcement agencies have been placed on maximum alert to maintain law and order. The PM warned that no group should be allowed to exploit the disaster through theft, robbery, hoarding, or the misappropriation of relief materials.

While officials from Chattogram reported that waterlogging is gradually easing, the situation in the Sylhet region is deteriorating due to a damaged embankment along the Manu River. Rangpur Division also faces a high risk of fresh waterlogging.

The Prime Minister stressed the need for transparency and accountability in relief distribution, urging officials to prioritize those genuinely affected. He ordered all authorities to keep personnel and equipment ready for every possible risk.

headline_marked: Dhaka to get 2 new plants: [[Waste-to-energy projects approved]] for Aminbazar and Matuail
headline: Dhaka to get 2 new plants: Waste-to-energy projects approved for Aminbazar and Matuail
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has directed the implementation of two major waste-to-energy plants in Dhaka, backed by investments from China and South Korea.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman held a meeting to expedite two waste-to-energy projects located at Aminbazar under the Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) and Matuail under the Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC).
China's CMEC Group will invest in the Aminbazar plant, which is designed to process approximately 3,000 tonnes of waste daily to generate 42.5 megawatts of electricity.
The Aminbazar project is expected to start supplying electricity to the national grid by August 2028 and will operate for the next 25 years.
South Korea's B&F Company will implement the Matuail project, processing 3,000 to 3,500 tonnes of waste daily to produce methane gas and approximately 81,000 megawatt-hours of electricity annually.
Beyond power, the Matuail plant will produce solar power, fertiliser, animal feed, and environmentally friendly eco-bricks.
The Prime Minister emphasised the need to complete both projects within the stipulated timeframe using the best available environmentally friendly technologies.
To speed up the process, he directed an inter-ministerial meeting involving the ministries of local government, power, and environment.
caption:
Dhaka is turning trash into treasure. Two massive waste-to-energy plants are coming to Aminbazar and Matuail!

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman held a meeting to expedite two waste-to-energy projects located at Aminbazar under the Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) and Matuail under the Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC).

China's CMEC Group will invest in the Aminbazar plant, which is designed to process approximately 3,000 tonnes of waste daily to generate 42.5 megawatts of electricity.

The Aminbazar project is expected to start supplying electricity to the national grid by August 2028 and will operate for the next 25 years.

South Korea's B&F Company will implement the Matuail project, processing 3,000 to 3,500 tonnes of waste daily to produce methane gas and approximately 81,000 megawatt-hours of electricity annually.

Beyond power, the Matuail plant will produce solar power, fertiliser, animal feed, and environmentally friendly eco-bricks.

The Prime Minister emphasised the need to complete both projects within the stipulated timeframe using the best available environmentally friendly technologies.

To speed up the process, he directed an inter-ministerial meeting involving the ministries of local government, power, and environment.
